title: Attention execution tiering + prefill memory adapter (dynamic kernel selection based on KV pressure)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: FlashAttention v2/v3 exhibit different memory footprints and stall characteristics across model shapes and sequence lengths. During high-concurrency prefill workloads we observe periodic OOMs or significant tail-latency spikes when the runtime sticks to a single kernel choice. Goal: implement an "execution tiering" mechanism plus a prefill memory adapter that dynamically chooses an attention kernel variant and prefill chunking strategy based on live KV-cache memory pressure and recent headroom estimates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime exposes a per-request decision hook that picks kernel variant (FA3-fast, FA2-stable, reduced-precision fallback) and prefill-chunk size based on memory headroom prediction. 2) Under controlled stress tests the change reduces 99.9th prefill latency by >=15% for our longest-context workloads without increasing average token cost by >5%. 3) No new OOMs in saturation tests across supported GPU families. 4) Production rollout via canary to 5% then 25% then 100% with automatic rollback if error-rate or latency SLOs breach thresholds.
proposal_summary: Add a lightweight in-runtime "prefill memory adapter" composed of: (a) a fast memory-pressure estimator sampling KV cache usage + allocator hints; (b) a small cost model mapping estimated headroom and seq_len to preferred kernel variant and chunk size; (c) a safelist/blacklist for models with known regressions; (d) telemetry hooks for decision and outcome. The adapter runs at request admission and returns signals used by the serving layer to select kernels and prefill schedule.
plan_steps: 1) Design API and decision contract (2 days) 2) Implement estimator and decision logic with feature flag (5 days) 3) Microbench harness for heterogenous shapes and hardware (3 days) 4) Integration tests and fault-injection (3 days) 5) Canary rollout and telemetry dashboards (4 days) 6) Gradual rollout + regression watch (ongoing)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Decision model could oscillate and cause kernel thrash. Mitigation: hysteresis window, rate limit decision changes per model instance. Risk: mispredicted headroom leads to suboptimal kernel causing latency regression. Mitigation: safe fallbacks, A/B rollback, and per-model safelists. Risk: telemetry volume increases. Mitigation: sampling and aggregation at runtime.
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit decision_reason, chosen_kernel, estimated_headroom_bytes, prefill_chunk_size, post-prefill-peak-usage, and outcome labels (ok/oom/evicted). Track 50/95/99/99.9 latency per kernel, OOM count, token-cost changes, and canary error budget spend.
testing_plan: Unit tests for decision logic, synthetic microbench across seq_len {128,512,2048,8192} and batch sizes, canary runs on dedicated pool with stress generator, fuzz allocator tests to simulate fragmented GPU memory, and long-running soak during canary to catch rare regressions.
rollout_strategy: Feature-flagged rollout: dev -> internal -> canary 5% (48h) -> canary 25% (72h) -> global. Automated rollback if 99.9th latency increases >10% or OOMs observed. Add manual gating for Dedicated customers.
notes_and_links: Design doc: /confluence/rw/RT-ExecTiering. Perf dashboard prototype: grafana/rw/prefill-adapter. PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5467 (estimator), /pull/5489 (integration). Related tickets: ENG-421999, ENG-100500.
